exposure: commonly used cross sectional neonatal charts
small for gestational age at birth
outcome: diagnosis of short term extrauterine growth restriction
cohort: The study included 80 moderate and late preterm infants (57% males) with a mean gestational age of 33.3 ± 2.2 weeks, without chronic or major morbidities.
finding: The employment of INTERGROWTH-21ST Preterm Postnatal longitudinal standards significantly reduced the diagnosis of short-term extrauterine growth restriction and lower loss of percentiles compared to commonly used cross-sectional charts, proving effective for monitoring growth.
